materiality_analysis.reason: The 2024 disclosure introduces a material change in the charge-off policy for consumer vehicle loans. Specifically, it adds a condition that loans are charged off 'when the borrower's ability to pay cannot be validated' and explicitly states they are charged off at 'estimated fair value less expected disposal costs'. The 2023 policy charged off at 'collateral values' upon 120 days past due or repossession. The addition of the 'ability to pay' validation trigger and the explicit definition of charge-off value (fair value less disposal costs) represents a change in the company's recognition and measurement methodology for credit losses.

comparisons.peer_summary: The company charges off unsecured installment loans at 120 days past due (DPD) or within 60 days of bankruptcy notification, while unsecured revolving and credit card loans are charged off at 180 DPD. Loans secured by non-real estate collateral are written down to estimated value less selling costs at 120 DPD, whereas real estate-secured loans are written down at 180 DPD, with specific exceptions for non-foreclosure decisions and bankruptcy filings.
comparisons.comparison: BAC and C both specify charge-off timing for unsecured installment and secured non-real estate loans at 120 days past due (DPD). BAC explicitly identifies consumer vehicle loans as being charged off at 120 DPD (upon repossession or validation failure), while C groups them under 'loans secured with non-real estate collateral' charged off at 120 DPD. Both banks also apply accelerated charge-off triggers within 60 days of bankruptcy notification. However, BAC places consumer vehicle loans on nonaccrual status at 90 DPD, whereas C's provided text details charge-off timelines for unsecured installment loans at 120 DPD and real estate-secured loans at 180 DPD, without explicitly stating the nonaccrual threshold for vehicle loans in the cited sentences.

sentences.text: Consumer vehicle loans are placed on nonaccrual status when they become 90 days past due, within 60 days after receipt of notification of bankruptcy or death or upon confirmation of fraud, unless the borrower's performance indicates that repayment is likely to occur.

These loans are charged off to the estimated fair value of the collateral less expected disposal costs when the loans become 120 days past due, upon repossession of the collateral, within 60 days after receipt of notification of bankruptcy or death or upon confirmation of fraud, and when the borrower's ability to pay cannot be validated.
• Unsecured installment loans are charged off at 120 DPD, or if in bankruptcy, within 60 days of notification of filing by the bankruptcy court, if earlier.
• Loans secured with non-real estate collateral are written down to the estimated value of the collateral, less costs to sell, at 120 DPD.

comparisons.peer_summary: Credit card loans are charged off when 180 days past due, and installment loans are charged off when 120 days past due.
comparisons.comparison: Both BAC and GS use a 120-day delinquency threshold for charging off installment-type loans (auto/installment). BAC charges off consumer vehicle loans at 120 DPD, while GS charges off installment loans at 120 DPD. GS additionally specifies that credit card loans are charged off at 180 DPD, a category BAC addresses separately (credit card loans charged off at 180 DPD in adjacent context, though not in the specific vehicle loan excerpt).

Installment loans were charged off when they were 120 days past due.

comparisons.peer_topic: Accelerated charge-off standards for specific consumer loan circumstances
comparisons.peer_summary: Certain consumer loans are charged off earlier than FFIEC standards, including collateral-dependent loans modified for borrowers in financial difficulty, loans to borrowers with known or highly certain losses (such as bankruptcy notification for real estate and auto loans within 60 days), and auto loans upon repossession.
comparisons.comparison: BAC and JPM both employ accelerated charge-off standards for auto loans triggered by bankruptcy notifications within 60 days. BAC places consumer vehicle loans on nonaccrual and charges them off within 60 days of bankruptcy notification, while JPM charges off or charges down auto loans within 60 days of receiving bankruptcy notification, noting this is earlier than standard FFIEC guidelines. Both also charge off auto loans upon repossession.

sentences.text: Consumer vehicle loans are placed on nonaccrual status when they become 90 days past due, within 60 days after receipt of notification of bankruptcy or death or upon confirmation of fraud, unless the borrower's performance indicates that repayment is likely to occur.

These loans are charged off to the estimated fair value of the collateral less expected disposal costs when the loans become 120 days past due, upon repossession of the collateral, within 60 days after receipt of notification of bankruptcy or death or upon confirmation of fraud, and when the borrower's ability to pay cannot be validated.

• Loans to borrowers who have experienced an event that suggests a loss is either known or highly certain are subject to accelerated charge-off standards (e.g., residential real estate and auto loans are charged off or charged down within 60 days of receiving notification of a bankruptcy filing).
• Auto loans upon repossession of the automobile.
